speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether MOE Kindergartens (MK) have in-house programmes for special needs children; (b) whether these programmes prepare their special needs students for mainstream Primary schools; and (c) how many special needs children are in the MK system currently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Not all these children have a formal diagnosis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Some were identified by our Kindergarten educators, who are equipped with basic awareness and strategies to support diverse learners in the classroom.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The type of support would vary depending on the needs of each child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Under these programmes, professionals such as Learning Support Educators and therapists provide intervention for identified children once or twice a week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This includes language and literacy support for children with learning needs and psychological support for children with behavioural needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE also provides Assistive Technology such as Frequency Modulation systems for children with hearing loss.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Some children who require medium to high levels of Early Intervention support also attend the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, EIPIC in short, outside of MKs to ensure that their developmental needs are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE Educational Psychologists work with our MKs to identify the needs of the children and design in-class strategies to support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MKs also work closely with parents to support their child and prepare them for transition beyond preschool, whether in mainstream or SPED schools.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I note from appeals from my residents, more families are asking for preschool placements for their special needs children and are being put on a waitlist or a special assessment before the child can be considered for school enrolment.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I understand for experts in the field, that is also important for intervention to take place at a young age for certain special needs conditions before former school begins.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that the MK system was put in place to prepare preschool children for formal education, would the Minister's assessment, be that the current spaces and in-school resources available for children with special needs, be sufficient for the Special Needs community?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Also, are our preschool sufficiently resource, especially with trained teaching staff and in-house therapist to handle such student loads?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: They would also have undergone training by the NIEC or the National Institute of Early Childhood Development or other training institutes on the skills required to identify and support children with developmental needs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Our MK Educators are supported by a Case Management Team set up in each MK to coordinate identification and support for children with developmental needs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The MK Case Management Team includes personnel, who receive more in-depth training including school Special Educational Needs Officers and our MK Special Educational Needs Coordinators.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Our MKs are also supported by MOE Educational Psychologists, who provide consultation on identification, referrals and advice on in-class strategies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I understand that children with special needs sometimes attend, not just their daily kindergartens, whether MOE or the anchor operators – like PCF, My First Skool and others.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But some of them also, because of their need, they attend the EIPIC programme, some specialised classes, and that is like once or twice a week.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I was recently told by some residents that the policy is such that if they receive EIPIC, which is early intervention support, then if they go to the kindergartens, which are also funded by MOE, then they would not receive support in the preschools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, my question to the Minister of State is, is that true?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And if that is true, could we consider looking into support for these children, so that they can receive an effective intervention and support on a daily basis?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, keep it to a short supplementary question, please.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Would the Ministry also be looking at the number of people on the waitlist?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Has it increased for special needs people wanting to enter the MK system over the last five years, for instance?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: And also, at the same time, would there also be numbers that you monitor in terms of the number of special needs people within the MK system?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As I have mentioned earlier on, MKs are part of the ecosystem of preschools in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Besides MKs, there are other preschools managed under MSF that cater to the needs of students, whether they hare normal or special needs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, I think it is important that we do not just look at the MKs by themselves, but look at how as a system as a whole, we can meet the needs and demands of the students.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, I think it is important that we look at this issue more holistically and not just look at the MOE system alone.
